name: Barycentric polynomial interpolation
definition: For distinct nodes x_i, set w_i=1/Π_(j≠i)(x_i−x_j), and P(x)=[Σ_i w_i y_i/(x−x_i)]/[Σ_i w_i/(x−x_i)]. Return y_i directly at x=x_i.
variables: x_i input nodes, y_i ordinates, w_i barycentric weights, P degree at most n−1
assumptions: A low-degree polynomial gives a useful interpolant on the given interval
limitations: High degree on equispaced nodes can yield oscillations; extreme spacing can also make weights ill-conditioned
failure_conditions: High degree on equispaced nodes can yield oscillations; extreme spacing can also make weights ill-conditioned
computation: O(n²) generic weight construction and O(n) per query

source.citation: SciPy maintainers’ reference, BarycentricInterpolator, Notes and boundary conditions. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.interpolate.BarycentricInterpolator.html

name: Natural cubic spline interpolation
definition: Choose piecewise cubic S with S(x_i)=y_i and continuity of S′ and S″ at interior knots. Enforce S″(x_0)=S″(x_(n−1))=0. For two knots this reduces to linear interpolation.
variables: S interpolant, x_i strictly increasing knots, y_i real ordinates
assumptions: At least two knots and natural endpoint conditions appropriate for the intended interpolation
limitations: Zero curvature at endpoints may be a poor approximation and does not generally imply linear extrapolation
failure_conditions: Zero curvature at endpoints may be a poor approximation and does not generally imply linear extrapolation
computation: O(n) spline construction with a tridiagonal solve and O(log n) interval lookup

name: Monotonicity-preserving cubic Hermite interpolation
definition: Let h_i=x_(i+1)−x_i, d_i=(y_(i+1)−y_i)/h_i. At interior knot i set m_i=0 when d_(i−1)d_i≤0; otherwise set (w₁+w₂)/m_i=w₁/d_(i−1)+w₂/d_i with w₁=2h_i+h_(i−1), w₂=h_i+2h_(i−1). At the left endpoint use r=((2h₀+h₁)d₀−h₀d₁)/(h₀+h₁), returning 0 if sign(r)≠sign(d₀), or 3d₀ if sign(d₀)≠sign(d₁) and |r|>3|d₀|, and r otherwise. Apply the reflected rule on the right. Join values and slopes by cubic Hermite segments. For two knots use the secant at both ends.
variables: x_i increasing knots, y_i sample ordinates, m_i knot derivative, d_i interval secant
assumptions: At least two knots, support restricted to knot span for the shape guarantee
limitations: Second derivatives can jump and interpolating noisy knots preserves their noise
failure_conditions: Second derivatives can jump and interpolating noisy knots preserves their noise
computation: O(n) slope construction and O(log n) interval lookup
